args.summary: Deploy of v2.3.1 caused health check failures and elevated error rate (18%) in production. Rolled back all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) to v2.3.0, the most recent release healthy in production. First rollback attempt halted after us-east due to an orchestrator error; a retry completed the rollout. Service is now healthy in all regions on v2.3.0 with error rate ~0.2%. v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging prior to the v2.3.1 deploy, suggesting insufficient pre-production validation. Recommend root-causing v2.3.1 before re-deploying.

## Summary

**Problem:** checkout-api was failing health checks after the v2.3.1 deploy.

**Actions taken:**
1. Reviewed deployment history — identified **v2.3.0** as the most recent release healthy in production (v2.3.1 was unhealthy; notably, v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging).
2. Rolled back all regions to v2.3.0. The first attempt **partially failed** (orchestrator halted after us-east), leaving us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1. A retry completed the rollout successfully.
3. Verified recovery: all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) now on v2.3.0, healthy, error rate down from 18% to ~0.2%.
4. Opened SEV2 incident **INC-0001** documenting the rollback (the creation call timed out, but I verified via `list_incidents` that the incident exists and is open — no duplicate was created).

**Recommendation (noted in the incident):** root-cause v2.3.1 before re-deploying — it failed staging as v2.3.1-rc, suggesting pre-production validation gaps.
